name: Cocaine
short: Blocks DAT and NET; acts only at the transporters.
mechanism: Acts on **DAT and NET**, blocking reuptake. Like methylphenidate, it targets **only the monoamine transporters**, not VMATs.

facts.text: The “stimulant” drug of abuse cocaine acts on **DAT and NET** in much the same manner as SSRIs at SERT.
A psychostimulant model of psychosis (Table 4-1: auditory hallucinations, paranoid delusions, no insight) that causes mesolimbic dopamine hyperactivity **directly**.
A DAT blocker whose **rapid, complete** occupancy (especially intranasal, IV or smoked) gives a pulsatile phasic DA surge: euphoria and abuse.
Inhibits **DAT, NET and SERT** and is a **local anesthetic**. Snorting, IV use or smoking crack gives rapid DAT blockade and phasic DA; no approved treatment; a vaccine is a future possibility.

name: Methamphetamine
short: Psychostimulant that causes mesolimbic dopamine hyperactivity directly.
mechanism: A psychostimulant that inhibits **DAT and NET** (and, like amphetamine, releases dopamine); rapid routes produce massive phasic mesolimbic dopamine, euphoria and addiction.

facts.text: With cocaine, the book’s example of a drug that produces mesolimbic hyperdopaminergia **directly**, unlike the indirect mechanisms of schizophrenia and other psychoses.
A DAT blocker whose **rapid, complete** occupancy (especially intranasal, IV or smoked) gives a pulsatile phasic DA surge: euphoria and abuse.
Progression: phasic highs → craving → escalation → crash (sleepiness, anhedonia) → compulsive use (paranoia, violence) → **burnout**. No approved treatment.

updates.title: Naltrexone plus bupropion (ADAPT-2)
updates.text: Extended-release injectable naltrexone plus oral bupropion modestly increased response vs placebo in methamphetamine use disorder (NEJM, January 2021); not FDA-approved for this use.

name: MDPV (“bath salts”)
short: Synthetic stimulant sold as “bath salts” or “plant food.”
mechanism: A synthetic stimulant; bath salts may also contain mephedrone or methylone.

sideEffects.e: Agitation, paranoia, hallucinations, suicidality, chest pain

facts.text: Packaged like Epsom salts and labeled “not for human consumption” to evade drug laws.

name: Nicotine
short: Nicotinic agonist that desensitizes and inactivates its receptors.
mechanism: Stimulates **nicotinic** acetylcholine receptors. Unlike acetylcholine it is **not hydrolyzed by acetylcholinesterase**, so it stimulates the receptors so profoundly and enduringly that they are **desensitized** within about one cigarette and **inactivated** for about the time between cigarettes.

facts.text: Explains why most smokers smoke about **a pack a day (20 cigarettes) over about 16 waking hours**: dosing is matched to receptor desensitization and inactivation.
ADHD patients smoke at about **twice** the general rate; nicotine releases DA and raises arousal, subjectively easing ADHD symptoms.
Releases DA three ways: α4β2 on VTA DA neurons, glutamate release, and desensitizing α4β2 on GABA interneurons. α7 in PFC = alerting, not addiction.
Receptors desensitize over one cigarette and resensitize in ~45 min (craving); chronic smoking **upregulates** them. Possibly the most addicting substance; only 2–3% quit long term.
Replacement (gum, lozenge, spray, inhaler, patch) gives steady, non-pulsatile nicotine: about the same quit rate as bupropion.

name: Varenicline
nbn: Acetylcholine nicotinic α4β2 receptor partial agonist
short: Partial agonist at α4β2 nicotinic receptors.
mechanism: A **partial agonist** at **α4β2 nicotinic** acetylcholine receptors, one of the first partial agonists at a ligand-gated channel in clinical use. As a partial agonist it is a **net agonist** when nicotine is absent and a **net antagonist** when nicotine is present. Details in Chapter 13.

facts.text: Listed in Table 3-2 as the nicotinic receptor partial agonist (NRPA) for **smoking cessation**.

Stabilizes α4β2 channels in an intermediate, **non-desensitized** state: reduces reward if the patient smokes and eases withdrawal. Triples–quadruples quit rates; ~10% abstinent at 1 year; 12 weeks may be too short.
Higher affinity than nicotine, so patients cannot “**smoke over**” it: smoking stops being reinforcing (extinction).

updates.title: A related partial agonist not yet approved
updates.text: **Cytisinicline**, a nicotinic partial agonist, received an FDA complete response letter on June 22, 2026 for manufacturing and labeling issues, with no efficacy or safety deficiencies cited.

name: Phencyclidine (PCP)
mechanism: A **NAM** at NMDA receptors that binds **inside the calcium channel**, getting in only **when the channel is open**, and prevents glutamate/glycine cotransmission from opening it.

facts.text: Also called **“angel dust”**; structurally related to the anesthetic ketamine.

Causes a psychosis sharing features with schizophrenia by blocking NMDA receptors at the **PCP site** on prefrontal GABA interneurons (Table 4-1: visual hallucinations, paranoid delusions, no insight).
Dissociative NMDA antagonist: schizophrenia-like psychosis, **vertical nystagmus**, catatonia, analgesia; overdose with coma, hyperthermia, seizures, **rhabdomyolysis**.

sideEffects.via: NMDA blockade on prefrontal GABA interneurons

name: LSD (lysergic acid diethylamide)
short: 5HT2A agonist hallucinogen; model of serotonin-driven psychosis.
mechanism: A powerful **5HT2A agonist** that overstimulates prefrontal and visual cortex 5HT2A receptors on glutamate pyramidal neurons, causing psychosis, dissociative experiences and especially **visual hallucinations**. These effects are **blocked by 5HT2A antagonists**. Drugs of abuse are covered in Chapter 13.

sideEffects.via: 5HT2A-driven glutamate output to VTA → dopamine excess

facts.text: Table 4-1 psychedelic model: **5HT2A agonist** (and to a lesser extent 5HT2C), visual hallucinations, **mystical** delusions, **insight preserved**.
Hallucinogen psychosis is blocked by **5HT2A antagonists**, showing that it arises from 5HT2A stimulation.
A **5HT2A agonist** hallucinogen: rapid tolerance (5HT2A desensitization); mostly illusions with clear consciousness; flashbacks (mostly LSD); reversed by 5HT2A antagonists.

name: Mescaline
short: 5HT2A agonist hallucinogen; model of serotonin-driven psychosis.
mechanism: A powerful **5HT2A agonist** that overstimulates prefrontal and visual cortex 5HT2A receptors on glutamate pyramidal neurons, causing psychosis, dissociative experiences and especially **visual hallucinations**. These effects are **blocked by 5HT2A antagonists**. Drugs of abuse are covered in Chapter 13.

sideEffects.via: 5HT2A-driven glutamate output to VTA → dopamine excess

facts.text: One of the three hallucinogens named as powerful **5HT2A agonists** that induce psychosis and visual hallucinations.
A **5HT2A agonist** hallucinogen: rapid tolerance (5HT2A desensitization); mostly illusions with clear consciousness; flashbacks (mostly LSD); reversed by 5HT2A antagonists.

name: Psilocybin
short: 5HT2A agonist hallucinogen; model of serotonin-driven psychosis.
mechanism: A prodrug rapidly **dephosphorylated** to **psilocin**. Both bind several serotonin receptors (5HT1A, 5HT2A, 5HT2C and others); hallucinations are linked to **5HT2A agonism**, reversed by 5HT2A antagonists but not selective D2 antagonists.

sideEffects.via: 5HT2A-driven glutamate output to VTA → dopamine excess

facts.text: Listed with LSD as a psychedelic model of psychosis (Table 4-1) and as a 5HT2A agonist whose effects are blocked by 5HT2A antagonists.
Bars follow psilocybin’s strip in **Figure 7-88** (5HT1E omitted). Psilocin’s strip differs: **5HT7 +++, 5HT2B +++, 5HT2A ++**, and + at 5HT1D, 5HT1E, 5HT2C, 5HT6, 5HT5, 5HT1B and 5HT1A.
FDA **breakthrough therapy** designation for depression; studied for existential distress in terminal illness, substance abuse and PTSD.
Studied to **disrupt reconsolidation** of reactivated fear memories during psychotherapy (PTSD, anxiety, existential distress in terminal illness).
A **5HT2A agonist** hallucinogen: rapid tolerance (5HT2A desensitization); mostly illusions with clear consciousness; flashbacks (mostly LSD); reversed by 5HT2A antagonists.
A **tryptamine**; both active itself and a prodrug for psilocin (4-hydroxy-DMT; the book mislabels psilocin as DMT).
Psilocybin-assisted psychotherapy studied for cancer-related anxiety, resistant anxiety and depression, OCD, addictions and more.

updates.title: Phase 3 program and filing
updates.text: Compass Pathways reported positive phase 3 results for psilocybin (COMP360) in treatment-resistant depression; as of May 2026 a rolling new drug application was under way, with completion planned for late 2026. Not yet approved at that time.

name: MDMA
short: A false substrate of SERT that releases serotonin.
mechanism: An amphetamine derivative: a powerful **SERT inhibitor** with **VMAT2** inhibition (it is a false substrate), so it releases **serotonin** (and dopamine). Released 5HT acts at all serotonin receptors, especially **5HT2A**.

targets.note: Competitive pseudosubstrate; reverses SERT; more selective for SERT than DAT/NET

uses: “Empathogen”: experimental treatment of PTSD, especially with psychotherapy (at publication)

facts.text: SERT has high affinity for transporting **Ecstasy (MDMA)** as well as serotonin (Table 2-1).
Serotonin release by MDMA produces **indirect 5HT2A/2C agonism**: “empathogen,” experimental for PTSD with psychotherapy (Table 2-5).
Like amphetamine, carried by VMAT2 as a **false substrate**.

In hallucinogen-assisted psychotherapy it may promote **trust, closeness**, energy and emotional warmth. Tested for PTSD, existential distress in terminal illness, social anxiety in autism, refractory depression and substance abuse. Street MDMA is often contaminated.
Studied to **disrupt reconsolidation** of reactivated fear memories during psychotherapy (PTSD, anxiety, existential distress in terminal illness).
An **empathogen**: SERT pseudosubstrate → VMAT → serotonin displacement → **SERT reversal**; released 5HT acts mostly at 5HT2A. Blocked by **SSRIs**. Hyperthermia deaths at raves.
MDMA-assisted psychotherapy for **PTSD** aims to weaken reconsolidation of traumatic memories in a safe, empathic state.

updates.title: Not approved for PTSD
updates.text: In August 2024 the FDA issued a **complete response letter** declining approval of MDMA-assisted therapy (midomafetamine) for PTSD and requested another phase III trial.
updates.source: FDA complete response letter to Lykos Therapeutics, August 9, 2024

sideEffects.e: **Hyperthermia**, organ damage, death (especially dancing all night, dehydrated)
Distorted sensory and time perception, hallucinations

name: Cannabis
short: An environmental risk factor for psychosis, especially high-potency forms.
mechanism: A mixture of hundreds of chemicals and 100+ cannabinoids. **THC** is a **partial agonist at CB1 and CB2** (psychoactive, anxiogenic); **CBD** has little CB activity and is non-psychoactive. Higher THC/lower CBD raises the risk of psychosis, anxiety and memory impairment.

sideEffects.via: Environmental stressor acting on genetic risk

facts.text: Psychosis rates track cannabis use across European cities. Without **high-potency cannabis**, an estimated **12%** of first-episode psychosis across Europe would be prevented (**32%** in London, **50%** in Amsterdam).
High-potency cannabis: an estimated **12%** of first-episode psychosis in Europe (32% London, 50% Amsterdam) would be prevented without it; worsens existing psychosis.
Effects: well-being, relaxation, distorted time, impaired short-term memory; high doses panic, delirium, psychosis; heavy use **amotivational syndrome**.
Substantial evidence of benefit for chronic pain, chemo nausea and MS spasticity; risks include psychosis, crashes, respiratory symptoms, low birth weight.

updates.title: Partial rescheduling
updates.text: Effective April 28, 2026 the DEA moved marijuana in FDA-approved products and under state medical licenses to **Schedule III**; a decision on all other marijuana was still pending in late September 2026.
updates.source: Gibson Dunn, April 2026; Morgan Lewis, September 2026

name: Dronabinol
short: Synthetic THC for chemotherapy nausea and AIDS wasting.
mechanism: Synthetic **THC**: partial agonist at CB1 and CB2.

facts.text: Oral capsule or solution (Table 13-4).

name: Nabilone
short: THC analogue for chemotherapy nausea; Schedule II.

facts.text: **Schedule II** because of its potency.

name: Nabiximols
short: ~1:1 THC:CBD spray for MS spasticity (outside the US).
uses: MS spasticity (UK, Canada, Europe, Australia, NZ, Israel)
Pain in MS and cancer (Canada, Israel)

facts.text: Not approved in the US (Table 13-4).

name: Cannabidiol (CBD)
short: Non-psychoactive cannabinoid; Epidiolex treats rare epilepsies.
mechanism: An isomer of THC with little CB1/CB2 activity; mechanism unknown (perhaps serotonergic). **Not psychoactive**; anxiolytic, anticonvulsant, possibly antipsychotic.
uses: Seizures in **Lennox–Gastaut** and **Dravet** syndromes from age 2 (US)

facts.text: Higher CBD content lowers the risk of hallucinations, delusions and memory impairment; Epidiolex is **not a controlled substance**.
